title: Traffic mirroring + split-test orchestration for hybrid deployments
creator: Maya Patel
description: Add a policy-driven orchestration layer that supports traffic mirroring (shadow), weighted split-tests (A/B), and staged promotion flows across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes while accounting for environment-specific constraints (networking, KMS, egress rules, and capacity). This ticket defines the design, accepts an implementation plan, and lays out rollout/rollback guardrails for the initial MVP.
background: Teams frequently need identical test behaviors (mirror, split, auto-rollback) when validating model updates, but the underlying environments impose different constraints: Hosted has soft quotas and cross-tenant routing, Dedicated enforces reserved GPU pools and tenancy isolation, Private runs inside customer VPCs with strict egress and KMS key access. Current rollout tooling is fragmented and requires manual config translation which causes drift, failed canaries, and delayed rollbacks.
goals: Provide a single declarative policy spec that expresses mirror, split, and promotion intent and compiles into environment-specific deployment primitives
Ensure safe default rollback behavior tied to SLO/regression signals
Enable observability signals (latency, error-rate, model-quality regressions) to be correlated across mirrored and split traffic
Prevent unsafe configurations (e.g., mirroring to private endpoints without network peering) with pre-deploy validation
non_goals: Full UI for composing experiments (this ticket focuses on API and orchestration primitives)
Replacing existing runtime scheduler; integration instead of rewrite
Support for multi-model ensembles in the first iteration
success_metrics: Reduction in manual translation tasks between environments by 80% for rollout configs
Time-to-detect regression during canary reduced to under 5 minutes for critical signals
90% of new model pushes use the declarative policy for at least one of mirror/split flows within 8 weeks of launch
Zero incidents caused by misrouted shadow traffic in Dedicated or Private during the first 3 months
acceptance_criteria: A declarative policy schema (YAML/JSON) exists and can express: mirroring to a target pool, weighted split to two variants, staged promotion percentages, and an auto-rollback policy bound to metric thresholds
Compiler/transpiler produces environment-specific manifests for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private with environment validation errors surfaced pre-apply
Runtime implements mirror plumbing that ensures no side-effects to production (read-only paths, masked logs) and tags mirrored requests for telemetry correlation
Auto-rollback triggers when threshold conditions are met (configurable thresholds) and creates an automated rollback job with an audit trail
Documentation and example configs for a model canary, a 10/90 split test, and a shadow validation pipeline are published
End-to-end test harness simulates traffic and validates rollback occurs in the staging environment
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Define policy schema and compiler with validation rules (2 sprints). Phase 2: Implement mirror plumbing and telemetry tagging for Hosted and Dedicated (2 sprints). Phase 3: Add Private wiring and VPC-aware validations, plus rollout/rollback automation (2 sprints). Phase 4: Integration tests, runbook, and docs (1 sprint). Deliver feature-flagged so we can opt teams in per-project.
architecture_decisions: Use a declarative policy-to-manifest compiler to avoid duplicating orchestration logic across controllers
Tag mirrored requests at the edge with x-redwood-mirror-id and enforce read-only headers to prevent writes during shadowing
Auto-rollback is enacted by reverting traffic weights to last known stable variant rather than instant full-service disable
Telemetry will use a shared correlation_id so mirrored and live traces can be joined in the console
rollout_strategy: Default: start with shadow-only validation for 48h, then a small weighted split (5/95) for 1 hour; if signals are stable, progress to 25/75 for 2 hours, then 50/50 for controlled exposure, and finally promotion. Auto-rollback evaluated continuously for critical metrics. Teams can override percentages per experiment.
rollback_criteria: 5xx rate increases by >2x baseline for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows
Median token generation latency increases by >250ms compared to baseline for 5 minutes
Model-quality regressions: failed prompts > 1% higher than baseline on the evaluation prompt-set
Manual abort by on-call engineer triggers immediate rollback
monitoring_and_alerting: Create dashboard showing live split percentages, variant latencies, error rates, and model-quality deltas
Alert if mirrored traffic is silently failing (e.g., >1% mirror ingestion errors),
Alert policy for auto-rollback events with links to audit log and last stable manifest
Synthetic tests (sample prompts) run against mirrored paths and reported as a separate 'shadow-liveness' metric
open_questions: How do we safely mirror requests that include customer data subject to different residency rules in Private deployments?
Should mirror traffic be rate-limited differently in Dedicated to avoid starving reserved capacity?
What is the canonical authorization model for invoking private model endpoints from the control plane?
notes: Implementation must coordinate with Security for KMS access patterns and Legal for PII in mirrored payloads. Work with Solutions Engineering to pilot with two customers (one Dedicated, one Private) during phase 3.
